Definition: properly, to hedge about (as with thorns), i.e. guard; generally, to protect, attend to, etc.
BiblicalUsage: Shamar is to keep, to guard, to watch over, and it is one of the tenderest words in the Bible. God put Adam in the garden to dress it and to keep it, and set the cherubim with a flaming sword to keep the way of the tree of life. The priest's blessing is the word itself, the LORD bless thee and keep thee, and the psalm promises that the LORD shall preserve thee from all evil, while the proverb says wisdom shall keep thee if thou forsake her not.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe keeping is God's work before it is ours, because He keeps us before He asks us to keep anything. The blessing is a promise before it is a command, and the heart that is kept by God learns to keep itself. That is why I pray the blessing over my own house, that the LORD would bless and keep us.
